title: Who Reaches the Third Friend First
statement:
Three friends stand on a straight street. Friend A is at position a, friend B at b, and friend C waits at c without moving.

A and B start walking towards C at the same moment and at the same speed. Return 1 if A reaches C first, 2 if B reaches C first, and 0 if they arrive at the same time.

examples.why: A is 4 steps away, B only 3.
Both are 5 steps away, on opposite sides.
A has the bigger position, but distance is what counts: A is 3 away, B is 2 away.

hints: Same speed means the arrival order depends only on one number per walker.
That number is the distance to C, which does not care about direction.
Compare |a − c| with |b − c|; equal means a tie.

explain.intuition: With equal speeds, time is proportional to distance, so compare distances. On a line the distance between two points is the absolute difference of their positions, which handles walkers on either side of C.
steps: Return 1 if da < db, 2 if db < da, else 0.
pitfalls: Using c − a without the absolute value. A walker standing to the right of C gets a negative "distance" and seems to win.
Comparing positions instead of distances, as in the third example.

solutions.title: Step both walkers
solutions.idea: Move both one step closer each tick and see who lands on C first.

solutions.title: Compare absolute distances
solutions.idea: Equal speed means the shorter distance wins.
